summary: Develop adaptive leadership, systems thinking, and decision skills for institutional uncertainty. Build practical tools in a five-day course.
lede: Adaptive Leadership and Systems Thinking for Volatile Institutional Contexts helps you distinguish technical fixes from challenges that require changed behaviours, authority patterns, and shared ownership. You will learn to see how decisions affect teams, services, partners, and communities through connected systems and feedback loops. Through institution-focused cases, decision laboratories, and structured reflection, you will practise diagnosing adaptive challenges, mapping relationships, prioritizing risks, aligning stakeholders, and testing decisions. You will also develop practical outputs such as causal loop diagrams, decision logs, risk registers, transformation roadmaps, and leadership briefings using Excel or Power BI templates.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who lead teams, programmes, services, or transformation portfolios through uncertainty and institutional complexity. It suits mid-level and senior decision-makers with operational experience who need a stronger method for coordinating people and choices across organizational boundaries.
prerequisites: You should have at least two years of experience supervising teams, managing programmes, or contributing to organizational transformation. No programming is required. Basic familiarity with budgets, operational risks, stakeholder coordination, and spreadsheet-based reporting will help you complete the exercises effectively. Advanced digital and complexity concepts receive conceptual and operational treatment, while systems mapping, risk logs, stakeholder plans, and dashboards receive guided hands-on practice.
